audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1 was given to Gnar at 7/10 while whys[0] ends 'the level-1 trade is genuinely even', and Level 6 was given to Gnar at 7/10 while whys[4] says his Q-slow and empowered autos walk you down and you have no answer without Rage.
audit.why: The packet chart reads Skill/Skill/Malphite for every remaining row on a 44.56% win rate over 1609 games — this is one of Gnar's worst lanes, and a 7/10 Level 6 row directly above 'his R catches your fragile Mini body' is the kind of contradiction that gets a page distrusted.
audit.corrected: Level 1 flipped to Skill at 5/10; Level 6 flipped to Malphite at 3/10 with phases[4].why rewritten around the ultimate. The chart now matches the packet on all seven rows.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere, and Granite Shield was described only as something that 'regenerates between trades'.
audit.why: Unstoppable Force is 130/115/100 — at rank 1 a spent R is over two minutes of free lane, which is the only real window Gnar gets in this matchup and the page never quantified it. Granite Shield absorbs up to 10% of his max health and recharges once he goes a few seconds unhit, which is why poke has to be chained rather than spaced out. Ground Slam is a 7-second cooldown.
audit.corrected: 130s written into spikes[1].text, whys[3], mid and phases[4].why; Granite Shield's 10% and its recharge-on-not-being-hit rule written into spikes[0].text and early; Ground Slam's 7s into early and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ground Slam does not appear anywhere on the page. Thunderclap is credited with granting bonus armour in three fields ('Thunderclap (W) bonus armor', 'his bonus-armor autos', 'Stack armor (Thunderclap W + first armor item)'). Unstoppable Force is called point-and-click and undodgeable.
audit.why: Ground Slam is the ability that makes this matchup bad and it was invisible: it deals magic damage scaled off his ARMOUR — so every armour item he buys is offence, not just defence — and it reduces attack speed, which is aimed squarely at the Hyper third-hit procs this page builds its entire plan on. Thunderclap in Riot's text creates aftershocks on his attacks; it grants no armour, so the reader was told to fear the wrong source. And Riot's Unstoppable Force text says he launches himself to a location — it is a travelling dash, not a point-and-click cast, so 'undodgeable' overstates it.
audit.corrected: Ground Slam's armour-scaling and attack-speed cut added to whys[5], spikes[2].text, early, mid, late and wants.foe[0]; the Thunderclap armour claim removed and replaced with its actual aftershock behaviour in wants.foe[2]; 'point-and-click and undodgeable' in whys[3] replaced with the cooldown and the knockup.
sources: enemyKit Ground Slam / Thunderclap / Unstoppable Force text

audit.whatIsWrong: early, mid and late are written in first person — 'Normally I feast on immobile bruisers', 'that's the exact form-RNG death I fear', 'My path is to never be the engage target'.
audit.why: The page speaks to the reader everywhere else; three paragraphs in the coach's own voice break it.
audit.corrected: All three converted to second person while I was rewriting them for Ground Slam.

edits.before: Mega + R against a wall is the best engage top lane owns. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Malphite's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Unstoppable Force lands at 6 on a 130s cooldown and knocks fragile Mini Gnar into the air. Never step up at 6 without full Rage banked.

edits.before: Unstoppable Force is point-and-click and undodgeable — it catches your fragile Mini body whenever Rage is down, with no Mega bulk to absorb it.
edits.after: Unstoppable Force is a 130-second launch that knocks up on arrival — it catches your fragile Mini body whenever Rage is down, with no Mega bulk to absorb it.

edits.before: Stacked armor makes your Boomerang and physical autos do almost nothing while his bonus-armor autos out-trade you the moment you step into range.
edits.after: Stacked armour blunts your Boomerang and autos, and Ground Slam turns that same armour into magic damage while cutting the attack speed Hyper needs.

edits.before: Boomerang plus the Hyper third-hit proc is your one poke window, and Hyper's third hit is MAGIC damage that ignores his armor stacking — chip him while his Granite Shield passive regenerates between trades.
edits.after: Boomerang plus the Hyper third-hit proc is your one poke window, and that third hit is MAGIC his armour never touches — but Granite Shield absorbs 10% of his max HP and recharges the moment you stop hitting him, so chain the poke.

edits.before: His Unstoppable Force R is a point-and-click unstoppable engage that knocks you up out of fragile Mini form — if Rage is down you have no Mega bulk, no Wallop stun, and no second Hop bounce to escape.
edits.after: Unstoppable Force arrives every 130 seconds at rank 1 and knocks you out of fragile Mini form into the air — if Rage is down you have no Mega bulk, no Wallop stun, and no second Hop bounce to escape it.

edits.before: His first armor item plus Thunderclap (W) bonus armor guts your physical Boomerang and autos, but his armor does nothing to your magic Hyper procs and zero to AP teammates.
edits.after: His first armour item guts your physical Boomerang and feeds Ground Slam, whose magic damage scales off his armour — but armour does nothing to your Hyper procs or to AP teammates.

edits.before: Normally I feast on immobile bruisers, but Malphite is the wrong target. Most of my Mini damage is physical Boomerang and autos, and he stacks armor — though my Hyper third-hit proc is MAGIC, so it still chips through his Granite Shield passive when it regenerates. I can win the level 1-2 trade by landing Boomerang plus the Hyper proc while his shield is down and his armor is bare, so do that and shove. But the moment he buys his first armor item my physical chip falls off, and his Seismic Shard Q-slow stops me kiting the way I want.
edits.after: Normally you feast on immobile bruisers, but Malphite is the wrong target. Most of your Mini damage is physical Boomerang and autos and he stacks armour — though the Hyper third-hit proc is MAGIC, so it still chips once Granite Shield's 10%-max-HP layer is broken. Win the level 1-2 trade by landing Boomerang plus the Hyper proc while that shield is down and his armour is bare, then shove. The moment he buys armour your physical chip falls off, and Ground Slam's attack-speed cut, up every 7 seconds, is aimed straight at the Hyper procs you rely on.

edits.before: This is where it slips. At 6 his Unstoppable Force is point-and-click — he doesn't dodge my telegraphed Wallop or eat a skillshot, he just R's and I'm airborne in fragile Mini form. If Rage is on cooldown when he commits, I have no Mega bulk, no Wallop stun, and no Hop bounce out — that's the exact form-RNG death I fear. Only step up when Rage is full so I can Wallop-stun him mid-engage or land my GNAR! wall-combo; otherwise respect the all-in and farm at max Boomerang range while my Hyper procs do the chip my autos can't.
edits.after: This is where it slips. At 6 Unstoppable Force launches him onto you and you are airborne in fragile Mini form. If Rage is on cooldown when he commits you have no Mega bulk, no Wallop stun and no Hop bounce out — the exact form-RNG death. It is 130 seconds at rank 1, so a spent R hands you a genuinely long window to take the lane back. Only step up with Rage full so a Wallop stun or the GNAR! wall-combo is live; otherwise farm at max Boomerang range while Ground Slam, up every 7 seconds, shaves your attack speed.

edits.before: It tilts further as he stacks pure armor and I'm a mostly-physical champ poking a wall. My Boomerang and autos do little into stacked armor, and in fights his R deletes my squishy Mini body before GNAR! ever matters. My path is to never be the engage target: hang back, let his R go onto someone else, then peel and clean up with a Mega Wallop or wall-pin. My magic Hyper damage and an AP teammate punish his armor-only build hard — but the straight lane and the straight 1v1 belong to him.
edits.after: It tilts further as he stacks pure armour and you're a mostly-physical champ poking a wall — and Ground Slam converts that armour straight back into magic damage on you. In fights his R deletes your squishy Mini body before GNAR! ever matters. Your path is to never be the engage target: hang back, let his R go onto someone else, then peel and clean up with a Mega Wallop or wall-pin. Your magic Hyper damage and an AP teammate punish an armour-only build hard — but the straight 1v1 belongs to him.

edits.before: Stack armor (Thunderclap W + first armor item) so your Boomerang and physical autos barely scratch him
edits.after: Stack armour so your Boomerang barely scratches him and Ground Slam's armour-scaled damage keeps growing

edits.before: Seismic Shard Q-slow you so you can't kite, then walk you down with his Thunderclap-empowered autos
edits.after: Seismic Shard steals your move speed for 3s so you can't kite, then Thunderclap's aftershocks walk you down

notes: The largest gap: Ground Slam was on neither layer. It scales its magic damage off his armour and cuts attack speed, which means (a) his armour items are offence too, and (b) the Hyper third-hit plan this page is entirely built on is the exact thing he shuts off. That reframes the lane more than anything else here. Thunderclap was also credited with granting bonus armour in three places; Riot's text gives it aftershocks on his attacks and no resistances at all. Two things I deliberately did not write, matching the mirror audit's call: the kit derives a 'grounding' flag on Seismic Shard and Ground Slam that Riot's own descriptions do not support, so no grounding claim appears in my edits; and the full-layer TL;DR's '%HP' claim about Gnar remains unverified. Finally, the packet's two suspectNames hits ('His Unstoppable Force', 'His Granite Shield') are both false positives caused by the leading possessive — the names are correct.
